# Pass 3: independent adversarial strict challenge

Use a third context and reviewer identity distinct from BOTH generation and
technical review. Read `docs/source-policy.md` and the applicable GH or AI
three-pass workflow; confirm the selected canonical credential ID and bound
policy. The retained `gh` filename is shared workflow compatibility, not source
approval. Read the actual guide and approved evidence again. AI-103/AI-200
technical evidence must be Microsoft Learn-only with complete credential-scoped
provenance. Try to disprove the key, not merely confirm pass 2.

Challenge any shortcut around observed course/path UID ancestry. A course bridge
must match `credential.officialUrls.training` and descend directly from the guide
or exact credential page; it cannot supply technical support or directly parent
documentation. Recheck the actual credential -> course -> path -> module -> unit
reference receipts rather than accepting an invented credential -> path link.

For EVERY option, including correct options, construct conditions under which
it could be correct. Find qualifying/contradictory official evidence. Record
`choiceId`, `claimRepresented`, `whyIncorrectInContext`, `couldBeCorrectWhen`,
`sourceIds` and `evidenceSummary` in `adversarial.optionChallenges`. For correct
options, explicitly explain why the answer is not incorrect in this context
and which conditions support it. For distractors explain the exact contextual
distinction; unrelated alternatives or a key requiring unmentioned conditions
fail. If no defensible sourced counterexample exists, reject or request manual
review rather than inventing a condition.

Record explicit `challenges` notes for scope, plan, role, preconditions,
featureStatus, sourceChanges, stemSufficiency, explanationBounds,
reasoningDepth and answerClues. Keep these shared field names; interpret them
against the documented product: plan/tier/edition and role/permission limits;
repository/organization/enterprise boundaries for GitHub, or
tenant/subscription/resource/project/service boundaries for Microsoft when
supported by the cited evidence. Do not invent restrictions to fill a checklist;
justify nonapplicability. Check grammar, length, negative wording, superficial
difficulty and reused concepts.

Score the exact candidate 0–4 on all 12 version-2 rubric criteria: alignment,
accuracy, scenarioCompleteness, answerUniqueness, distractorPlausibility,
distractorEvidence, documentationStrength, citationSpecificity,
difficultyAuthenticity, explanationQuality, originality,
clarityAccessibility. Accuracy, answerUniqueness, documentationStrength and
citationSpecificity must be 4; distractorEvidence >=3; no zero; sum >= the
manifest threshold (at least 44/48). These are YOUR actual evidence-based
scores, not a conversion from an old rubric or a target to backfill.

Write the actual adversarial timestamp strictly after pass 2, reviewer, verdict,
unchanged question/objective hashes and question-specific quality notes. Never
schedule, backdate or manufacture a clock to satisfy ordering.
Write the rubric at the same timestamp/reviewer in encounter metadata.
Only after all checks pass may the final question become verified with
requiresManualReview false. The final package and consolidated ledgers must
contain your full per-option independent attestation at this same date and
verdict. Rejected/manual/stale records remain reportable with exact reasons.
Preserve old reviews; never rebind hashes after a rewrite. Existing AI-103
two-pass records receive no inherited three-pass approval or rubric conversion.
Review success alone does not open a credential: beta and pending/unverified
remain sealed, including when beta identity has been freshly verified.
